finalAnswer:
This is an analytical model of the declared design in `solution.architecture.json`, not a load test. **20x does not hold: the design saturates at roughly 2.5x baseline.**

Baseline ingress is 400 rps, so 20x is 8,000 rps against a modelled ceiling of **1,000 rps** (first limiter: the Lambda worker tier).

| | 1x (400 rps) | 20x (8,000 rps) |
|---|---|---|
| Critical path P50 | 80 ms | **1,007 ms** |
| Critical path P99 | 308 ms | **4,566 ms** |
| Headroom | 2.5x | **0.125x** |
| Saturated components | none | 5 |

Where it breaks, in order of overload:

- **ECS Fargate — 444%.** Autoscale caps at 6 × 300 rps = 1,800 rps, so it serves 1,800 of the 8,000 offered.
- **Cognito — 400%** and **S3 — 160%.** Both sit on `users`/`cdn` fan-out and take the full 8,000 rps.
- **Aurora — 222%**, with a **self-sustaining retry storm**: the 800 ms timeout plus 2 retries on `app-db` amplifies offered load 1.85x, which the model reports as not settling.
- **Lambda — 180%**, with the SQS backlog growing **800 messages/s** — async work falls behind indefinitely rather than failing requests.

Two things to read carefully: "ingress traffic lost: 0%" means the edge keeps accepting everything (CloudFront 16%, ALB 40% utilised) — the surge shows up as queueing and latency, not as rejected traffic at the door. And Aurora is still a single instance, so it is a SPOF under load as well as at rest.

Cache changes the picture materially. Rerunning with an 80% cache hit ratio keeps ECS Fargate *and* Aurora inside capacity; the ceiling moves to Cognito at 2,000 rps. The default run assumes a 0% hit ratio, i.e. no cache benefit at all.

Caveats that affect the conclusion: 27 inputs are authored, 28 assumed from role defaults — including the capacities of the limiter itself (Lambda 1,000 rps), Cognito (2,000 rps) and S3 (5,000 rps). Cost at 20x models to ~$9,378/month, but only 4 of 10 components carry prices. Give me real capacity figures for the worker, Cognito and S3 tiers and I'll rerun.

You can also try this yourself in [the architecture page](<temp>\project\solution.html) — the Workbench button opens a Simulate mode with the load multiplier and fault controls.
